title: Revealing Long-context Potential of Attention Heads via Frequency Kernels
claim: Heads with high long-context potential concentrate energy in few low frequencies, and amplifying those frequency kernels improves long-context performance.
layout: 2 panels: (a) math derivation left, (b) head-to-kernel flow with plots right
description: Panel (a), on the left, shows a matrix-factorization derivation of the attention score with RoPE. Query, W_Q, rotation matrices R(i) and R(j)^T, W_K^T and Key are drawn as color-striped matrices. Below them, equations lead to two red dashed boxes. One is labeled 'Frequency components' and the other 'Frequency kernels at distance i−j'. A rainbow bar underneath runs from low to high RoPE frequency. Panel (b), on the right, shows a multi-head attention block in green, with Head1 and Head2 extracted as stacked kernel squares. Two numbered line plots with red and gray curves show that energy concentrates at low frequency and that a few frequencies dominate. A red amplified kernel feeds a bar chart comparing Original and Amplified performance at context lengths from 4k to 128k.
caption: (a) By pre-computing the kernels of attention heads at different RoPE frequencies and distances, we can analyze the properties
abstract: Large language model (LLM) exists a subset of attention heads that are highly responsible for long-context processing. Existing work has identified different long-context heads in models, but their detection methods mainly rely on model inference on actual long texts and do not analyze the inherent properties of the head parameters. In this paper, we use kernel methods to analyze static \textit{frequency kernels} formed by different rotation frequency components of attention heads, and we design a Long-context Potential Score (LPS) to measure the potential of attention heads in processing long contexts. Kernels of heads with high LPS exhibit concentrated low-frequency energy and low effective rank, which allow them to effectively capture highly specialized information from distant contexts. Experiments and analysis on long-context tasks and model behaviors show that the LPS metrics can well reflect the actual capability of heads on long contexts. Furthermore, by simply amplifying low-frequency kernels of heads with high retrieval potential, we can further improve model's performance on long-context tasks. Our metrics and head enhancement methods are fully static and offline, and they can be quickly conducted under low-resource constraints. Code is publicly available at here .
